蔽.meaning: A fox spills a pot of blue paint all over the lawn. Before the owner gets home, it drags every old <part>rag</part> from the shed outside and pats fresh <part>grass</part> clippings on top until not one splash shows. The owner finds a very proud fox sitting on a perfect <kanji>cover</kanji>.
蔽.on: Then the fox hides the empty paint pot deep in a pile of <sound>hay</sound>.
蔽.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>, <sound>oh</sound>!' groans the owner, lifting one rag: bright blue grass underneath.

謁.meaning: On a crowded beach, a crab crowns itself king beneath a little striped <part>sunshade</part>. One by one, other crabs scuttle up, bow low and make a nervous <part>speech</part> asking for a bigger rock pool. The king listens, clicks a claw and grants each one an <kanji>audience</kanji>.
謁.on: Each visitor leaves a tiny <sound>etch</sound>ing of the king, scratched into a shell with one claw.

諧.meaning: At a meeting of the pond, every frog croaks its own <part>speech</part> at once: bigger lily pads, more flies, no herons! It's chaos, until one old toad croaks a single low note and <part>all</part> of them join in on it. The whole pond hums in perfect <kanji>accord</kanji>.
諧.on: The note is so loud that a <sound>ki</sound>te over the pond wobbles on its string.
諧.kun: <sound>Cu</sound>nning but outvoted, the heron flaps off to the <sound>nu</sound>t trees, and the frogs' wish comes true.

頰.meaning: A <part>large</part> walrus blows up a giant <part>rubber duck</part> float for his <part>twins</part>, puffing until his face swells round as two melons. Just before the duck is full, the twins each poke one side, and whoosh! The air bursts back out of his <kanji>cheeks</kanji>.
頰.on: Gasping, he names the duck after his favourite city, '<sound>Kyo</sound>to!', puffing out the start so long his whiskers wobble.
頰.kun: To cool him down, the twins spray his red face with the garden <sound>ho</sound>se.

璽.meaning: The emperor's seal goes missing. The palace cook finally finds it on her <part>spice rack</part>, between the cinnamon and the paprika, its red <part>jewel</part> handle dusted in pepper. All year every decree comes out stamped with a smell that makes the court sneeze: the <kanji>imperial seal</kanji>.
璽.on: She races it back to the throne room in a muddy <sound>jee</sound>p, sneezing all the way.

籠.meaning: A shy <part>sea serpent</part> wants to visit the beach market, so it weaves strips of <part>bamboo</part> with the tip of its long tail all night. At dawn it slithers ashore with seaweed sandwiches piled in the biggest <kanji>basket</kanji> anyone has ever seen.
籠.on: On top of the sandwiches it lays one red <sound>ro</sound>se, for whoever is brave enough to say hello.
籠.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>lm swimmer in <sound>go</sound>ggles is the first to wave back.
